A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SQDF research and contain 36 pages, including Appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original text-to-image fine-tuning, online black-box optimization, ablation, and SDXL experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the comparisons in Tables 1–4 and the main-text and appendix figures.

M1.justification: The SQDF objective, reparameterized gradient, discount factor, consistency model, and replay-buffer procedure are unchanged. Section 4 and both algorithms in Appendix H are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same toy distribution, animal prompts, HPDv2 prompts, and black-box optimization tasks. The new introductory mention of SDXL describes experiments already present in v2’s Appendix F.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: DDPO, DRaFT, ReFL and their reported KL variants; PPO+KL and SEIKO variants for black-box optimization; and pretrained SDXL and DRaFT in Appendix F.

E3.justification: The evaluation settings in Section 5 and Appendices D–F are unchanged, including prompt splits, metrics, training budgets, 32 evaluation images per prompt, and the 15,360-query black-box budget.

E4.justification: Both retain identical component ablations, DDIM-versus-consistency comparisons, replay-prioritization and discount-factor analyses, collapse examples, and within-prompt qualitative comparisons in Section 5.3 and Appendices C and E.

E5.justification: The three-random-seed statements in Section 5 and Appendix F are unchanged. Table 1 retains the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, and graphical uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4, plotted results, and qualitative samples are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports the same SDXL aesthetic scores of 7.86 for SQDF and 7.18 for DRaFT in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, approximations, and derivations are unchanged, including the soft-policy and Bellman derivations in Appendix A and discounted soft-Q bounds in Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, SQDF contributions, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims. The introduction now mentions the existing SDXL evaluation and shortens its black-box comparison sentence; the substantive efficacy and comparative claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of credit assignment, consistency-model accuracy, replay-buffer benefits, and reward–diversity trade-offs are identical. No substantive applicability qualification, failure condition, or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, timing, and data-processing instructions. The code-access statement and Appendix H pseudocode are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography contain the same works and positioning. Podell et al. (2023), newly mentioned in the introduction, was already cited in Appendix F and listed in v2’s bibliography.

P1.justification: v3 briefly revises the introduction to mention SDXL and removes 'compared to baselines' from its final sentence. It adds an acknowledgment and replaces the preprint header with an ICLR 2026 publication header; the remaining narrative structure is unchanged.

P2.justification: The publication header and first-page version stamp change. The acknowledgment shifts the LLM-use disclosure and bibliography across pages 10–13. All figures and tables retain their content, formatting, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the introduction slightly more complete by mentioning the SDXL experiments already reported in v2’s Appendix F. The acknowledgment and publication-format updates accompany unchanged methods, evidence, theory, and reproducibility information, yielding no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
